segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in subsection 2 [(2) appended below],
the driver of a vehicle
shall not drive upon or within any sidewalk area
except at a permanent or temporary driveway or alley entrance.
A person who violates this subsection is guilty of a misdemeanor.
The provisions of subsection 1 do not apply to a vehicle that is powered solely by electricity and designed to travel on three wheels when such a vehicle is operated:
(a) As an authorized emergency vehicle;
(b) By an officer or other authorized employee of a law enforcement agency,
as that term is defined in NRS 239C.065 [DEF-NRS-239C-065],
in the course of his or her official duties; or
(c) By a security guard,
as that term is defined in NRS 648.016 [DEF-NRS-648-016],
in the course of his or her official duties.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'; 'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'). 'Driver' is no aggregate: the contract excludes 'a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle', so the driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency). Same words mapped the same way by NRS_484B_113_2 and LVMC_11_20_060_o1.

rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (… sidewalk …)' carries 'upon or within'. st.sidewalk: 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line', which is DEF-NRS-484A-240 'that portion of a highway between the curb lines … and the adjacent property lines intended for the use of pedestrians'; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk' does not apply, the words name the sidewalk area. 'drive' is the vehicle's controlled motion: the vehicle is not at rest, the negation of drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation … speed at or below a tolerance'), whatever controls it.

st.driveway_or_alley_entrance: 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there' does not apply since the words except driveway and alley entrances alike. 'permanent or temporary' admits both, so the kind is read whatever its permanence. rel.occupies anchors it: the vehicle's footprint overlaps the entrance region while on the sidewalk.

Nearest atoms only (gap). ru.motorcycle is a 'motor vehicle on two or three wheels ridden astride' and states neither electric propulsion nor that the vehicle is built for three wheels; ru.electric_scooter is 'a standing or seated electric scooter with handlebars' with no wheel count. Neither carries 'powered solely by electricity and designed to travel on three wheels'.

The table admits 'authorized emergency vehicle' as DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); ru.aggregate carries membership. 'Operated as' one is that membership, not a responding role, which the aggregate's contract excludes.

Nearest atoms only (gap). The words name the person operating, by role: an officer or authorized employee of a 'law enforcement agency', borrowed from DEF-NRS-239C-065: '(2) A metropolitan police department; (3) A police department of an incorporated city; or (4) The Department of Public Safety.' ru.emergency_vehicle (kind police) is 'vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency' and ru.official_vehicle a vehicle 'in official or contracted road service': both are classes of the vehicle, not the role of the person at its controls.
Nearest atoms only (gap). 'in the course of his or her official duties' is whether the officer acts on duty; no atom carries an operator's duty status, and a vehicle class is not it.

Nearest atom only (gap). 'Security guard' borrowed from DEF-NRS-648-016: 'means a person employed as a watchman, guard, security consultant, patrol officer or in any other similar position.' It is the role of the person operating; ru.official_vehicle ('a vehicle in official or contracted road service') is a vehicle class and no security role.
Nearest atom only (gap). The guard's being on duty is an operator's duty status, which no atom carries.

compositions.quote: (2) A metropolitan police department; (3) A police department of an incorporated city; or (4) The Department of Public Safety.
means a person employed as a watchman, guard, security consultant, patrol officer or in any other similar position.

residues.why: Points to subsection 2, which is appended to this same law line and carried by its own exception spans s6-s13; the duty is the same whether or not these words are read.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) whose footprint overlaps a sidewalk region (rel.occupies, st.sidewalk), and it is not an electric three-wheeled vehicle operated as an authorized emergency vehicle, by a law-enforcement officer or employee on duty, or by a security guard on duty (s6-s13, carried by the gap atoms).
obligation: At every observation at which the subject's footprint overlaps a sidewalk region and the subject is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), its footprint also overlaps a driveway or alley entrance region (st.driveway_or_alley_entrance); otherwise violated.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

'drive' is read as the vehicle not being at rest while on the sidewalk; a vehicle standing still there is not driving at that observation (its earlier motion onto the sidewalk is judged at the observations where it moved).

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not follow another vehicle
more closely than is reasonable and prudent, having due regard for the speed of such vehicles and the traffic upon and the condition of the highway.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'; 'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'Driver' is a relational role the contract excludes from membership; it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Same words as 'The driver of a vehicle' (LVMC_11_20_060_o1).

'follow another vehicle': rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction', with the other road user ahead of the subject; the other is a vehicle, ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, never a class list.

operationalizations.standard: more closely than is reasonable and prudent, having due regard for the speed of such vehicles and the traffic upon and the condition of the highway
operationalizations.convention: Car-following stopping-distance convention: the longitudinal component of the body gap to each vehicle ahead in the lane (rel.surface_gap) is at least the subject's speed times a time headway, plus the difference of the two vehicles' braking distances (subject speed squared minus the followed vehicle's speed squared, over twice a braking deceleration). The speeds of both vehicles enter the bound by degree; the condition of the highway selects the headway and the deceleration: icy or snow-covered surface (env.ice_or_snow) the _ice pair, else a wet surface or falling rain (env.wet_road or env.precipitation) the _wet pair, else the _dry pair. Headways from the driver-manual following-time rules; decelerations from tyre-road friction tables.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle).
obligation: For every road user b that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane): the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap(subject, b) is at least speed(subject) × H + (speed(subject)² − speed(b)²) / (2 × D), where H and D are p.following_headway_ice and p.following_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_headway_wet and p.following_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.following_headway_dry and p.following_decel_dry (written with Term.cond). Violated at an observation where some such b is closer.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

'the traffic upon … the highway' is read only through the followed vehicle and its speed, the part of the traffic the following distance answers to; the density of other traffic is not read. 'the condition of the highway' is read only through its surface (wet, icy or snow-covered, or rain falling); grade, curvature and surface damage are not read.

segmentation.text: The driver of any truck or combination of vehicles 80 inches or more in overall width,
which is following a truck, or combination of vehicles 80 inches or more in overall width,
shall, whenever conditions permit,
leave a space of 500 feet so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger,
but this shall not prevent a truck or combination of vehicles from overtaking and passing any vehicle or combination of vehicles.
This subsection does not apply to any vehicle or combination of vehicles while moving on a highway on which there are two or more lanes available for traffic moving in the same direction.

elements.justification: 'truck' and 'combination of vehicles' are admitted aggregates (DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck, 'every motor vehicle which is used for the transportation or delivery of goods with a body built and designed for that purpose'; DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles, 'two or more vehicles coupled together'), claimed through ru.aggregate. '80 inches or more in overall width': kin.extent, 'the body's size along its axes … a formula reads the full length, width and height', the full width compared with the stated figure. 'Driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'following': rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction', the followed road user b ahead of the subject with no other road user between them in that lane (the one it immediately follows). b is a truck or a combination of vehicles (the admitted aggregates) whose full width (kin.extent) is at least the stated figure.

'leave a space of 500 feet': rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies … its longitudinal and lateral components', the longitudinal component to the followed vehicle at least the stated figure. The words 'so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger' state why the space is left; the duty is the stated space itself (narrowing).

'overtaking and passing any vehicle or combination of vehicles': drv.interaction.overtake_pass, 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear … comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it', with a the subject and b any road user that is a vehicle or a combination of vehicles (admitted aggregates). The pass is under way where its recognition falls within the window ahead of length p.overtake_window, the concept's own recognition window.

'a highway on which there are two or more lanes available for traffic moving in the same direction': st.lane_adjacency, 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction', read on the lane (st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') the subject occupies (rel.occupies); the count is at least the stated figure. 'any vehicle or combination of vehicles' is the subject already bound by g1.

operationalizations.convention: Conditions permit the space where the followed vehicle has been the subject's immediate leader in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, no other road user between) and neither vehicle has been at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt) at every observation of the window behind of length p.truck_space_open_time: the time a heavy vehicle needs to open the space behind a leader by easing off a few miles per hour. A leader that has just come ahead of the subject, or a queue at rest, does not yet permit it.

applicability: The subject is a truck or a combination of vehicles (either admitted aggregate) whose full width (kin.extent) is at least 80 inches, and the lane it occupies (rel.occupies, st.lane) does not count two or more lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count).
obligation: For every road user b that is a truck or a combination of vehicles of full width at least 80 inches, ahead of the subject in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with no other road user ahead of the subject and behind b in that lane: either (i) conditions do not permit — it is not the case that, at every observation of the window behind of length p.truck_space_open_time, b was so the subject's immediate leader and neither the subject nor b was at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, p.halt_speed_tolerance); or (ii) the subject is overtaking and passing — within the window ahead of length p.overtake_window some road user c that is a vehicle or a combination of vehicles is overtaken and passed by the subject (drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, c) with p.overtake_window, p.overtake_same_direction_cos); or (iii) the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap(subject, b) is at least 500 feet. Violated where none holds.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the truck's or combination's conduct whoever controls it.
'so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger' states the purpose of the space; the duty is the stated space, and whether an overtaking vehicle is present is not read.

'whenever conditions permit' is a catch-all read only through the leader having been the subject's immediate leader, both moving, for the window that opening the space takes; other conditions (grade, traffic behind) are not read.

segmentation.text: Motor vehicles being driven
upon any highway
outside of a business district
in a caravan or motorcade
whether or not towing other vehicles,
shall be operated to allow sufficient space between each such vehicle or combination of vehicles
so as to enable any other vehicle or combination of vehicles to enter and occupy such space without danger.

elements.justification: 'Motor vehicles' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), claimed through ru.aggregate. 'being driven' is the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).
st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', DEF-NRS-484A-095's highway; rel.occupies anchors it to the subject's footprint. Same words mapped the same way by LVMC_11_22_020.

Nearest atoms only (gap smoke31-1111-0039:G17, kept). rel.ahead_behind_in_lane and rel.same_direction state that vehicles follow one another in one direction, which any vehicles in traffic do; neither carries membership of an organized caravan or motorcade.

'space between each such vehicle or combination of vehicles': rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', longitudinal component, between the subject and the member of the same caravan ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane). 'such vehicle' is a motor vehicle of the caravan, 'combination of vehicles' the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles, a motor vehicle with what it tows being one body.

operationalizations.standard: sufficient space … so as to enable any other vehicle or combination of vehicles to enter and occupy such space without danger
operationalizations.convention: The space between caravan members is sufficient where its longitudinal body gap is at least the length of a design combination vehicle plus a time headway in front of it and one behind it at the subject's speed: p.caravan_entry_vehicle_length + 2 × speed(subject) × p.caravan_entry_headway. The design vehicle is the largest combination the words' 'any other vehicle or combination of vehicles' admits; the headway is the following-time rule.

residues.why: Towing or not towing other vehicles adds no restriction: the duty binds a caravan member either way.

applicability: The subject is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) occupying a highway (rel.occupies, st.highway), the reading does not place it in a business district (not asm.business_district), and it travels as a member of a caravan or motorcade (gap smoke31-1111-0039:G17).
obligation: For every road user b that is a member of the same caravan and ahead of the subject in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap(subject, b) is at least p.caravan_entry_vehicle_length + 2 × speed(subject) × p.caravan_entry_headway; violated where it is less.

narrowings.why: 'being driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

gaps.proposal: `ru.procession_member` | a road user travelling as a member of an organized group of vehicles proceeding together in a caravan or motorcade, as the source records the group; a **group** attribute identifies the procession, so that two members of one procession are told apart from two vehicles that merely follow each other; decides which road users owe the caravan spacing and between which of them it is measured **Not a stand-in for:** following (`rel.ahead_behind_in_lane`) or travelling in the same direction (`rel.same_direction`) — vehicles following one another in traffic are no procession | general

segmentation.text: A person
shall not open the door of or board or alight from
the side of a vehicle which is closest to passing traffic
in such a manner as to interfere with
moving vehicular traffic.

elements.justification: The person who opens a door, boards or alights is not observable as such; the conduct is the door of a vehicle opening, so the rule judges the vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) whose door it is. Same words mapped to the vehicle aggregate by LVMC_11_22_010.
sig.door_open: 'a door open; side ∈ {traffic, curb}'. Opening the door, boarding and alighting through that side all show as the door on that side being open.
'the side of a vehicle which is closest to passing traffic' is the value side = traffic of sig.door_open; the vehicle is the subject (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle).

'vehicular traffic': road users that are traffic (admitted DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'vehicles and other conveyances … using any highway for purposes of travel') and vehicles (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle); 'moving': not at rest, the negation of drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation').

operationalizations.standard: in such a manner as to interfere with
operationalizations.convention: While the traffic-side door is open, a moving vehicle of the traffic is interfered with where it touches the subject (rel.contact) or passes alongside it (rel.longitudinal_overlap: the two projections on the subject's heading share length) with a lateral body gap (rel.surface_gap, lateral component) no greater than the lateral reach of an open side door, p.door_swing_reach: it then drives through the space the open door takes.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle and its door on the side closest to passing traffic is open (sig.door_open side traffic).
obligation: No road user c that is traffic and a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) is in contact with the subject (rel.contact), or alongside it (rel.longitudinal_overlap: projections share length) with the lateral component of rel.surface_gap(subject, c) at most p.door_swing_reach; violated where one is.

narrowings.why: 'A person' who opens the door, boards or alights is read through the vehicle's traffic-side door being open: who is at the door is not observable.
Boarding and alighting are read through the open traffic-side door they pass through; boarding or alighting from a vehicle side that has no door is not read.
Interference is read as a moving vehicle touching the subject or passing alongside within the open door's reach; a moving vehicle that brakes or swerves earlier to avoid the door is not read.

segmentation.text: A person
shall not leave open a door on the side of a vehicle which is closest to passing traffic
longer than is necessary for immediate loading or unloading of passengers or cargo.

elements.justification: The person who leaves the door open is read through the vehicle whose door it is: ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the same mapping LVMC_11_22_010 gives 'A person'.

sig.door_open: 'a door open; side ∈ {traffic, curb}'; 'the side of a vehicle which is closest to passing traffic' is side = traffic. 'leave open' is the door staying open over time, read by the standard's window.

operationalizations.standard: longer than is necessary for immediate loading or unloading of passengers or cargo
operationalizations.convention: A traffic-side door left open at every observation of the window behind of length p.traffic_side_door_max_open has been open longer than immediate loading or unloading needs: the curbside dwell of a passenger pick-up or a hand-carried delivery.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle and its door on the side closest to passing traffic is open (sig.door_open side traffic).
obligation: It is not the case that the subject's traffic-side door has been open at every observation of the window behind of length p.traffic_side_door_max_open (holdsFor time); violated where it has.

narrowings.why: 'A person' who leaves the door open is read through the vehicle's traffic-side door state.
Whether loading or unloading is going on, and whether of passengers or of cargo, is a purpose not observable; the time necessary is read as one duration bound on the door being continuously open.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car stopped at the curb keeps its traffic-side door open for five minutes.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car stopped at the curb opens its traffic-side door for 15 s while a passenger gets out, then closes it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car stopped at the curb with its traffic-side door closed and its curb-side door open.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car stopped at the curb; the source declares sig.door_open absent.

param_proposals.name: p.traffic_side_door_max_open
param_proposals.convention: the longest time a traffic-side door stays open for immediate loading or unloading: a passenger pick-up or drop-off dwell at the curb
param_proposals.source: curbside passenger-loading dwell studies

segmentation.text: Drivers of vehicles proceeding in opposite directions
shall pass each other keeping to the right,
and
upon highways having width for not more than one line of traffic in each direction,
each driver shall give to the other at least one-half of the paved portion of the highway
as nearly as possible.

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, for the subject and the other. 'proceeding in opposite directions': rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing', with its tolerance; its exclusion concerns 'the direction a road user approaches from' an intersection, which these words do not name: they name two vehicles meeting on a way. 'proceeding': the subject is not at rest (negation of drv.motion.complete_halt). 'Drivers' is read through the vehicles' controlled motion.

'pass each other': the two are alongside, rel.longitudinal_overlap, 'the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share'. 'keeping to the right': each keeps the other on its left, rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for "on the right of" …)', its lateral component on the subject's left. Both occupy the same highway (rel.occupies, st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'), so a vehicle on another way is not met.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance).
obligation: For every road user c that is a vehicle, occupies a highway region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.highway), is oncoming to the subject (rel.oncoming with p.oncoming_heading_cos) and is alongside it (rel.longitudinal_overlap: the projections share length): c lies on the subject's left (the lateral component of rel.bearing(subject, c) is to the left). Violated where such a c lies on the subject's right.

narrowings.why: 'Drivers' is read through the vehicles' controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls them.
Passing each other is read as the two vehicles being alongside on the same highway; vehicles on different ways are not read as passing each other.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a two-way road, an oncoming car passes the moving subject car on the subject's right side.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: On a two-way road, an oncoming car passes the moving subject car on the subject's left side.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car is at rest at the curb while an oncoming car passes.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: An oncoming car passes the moving subject car; the source declares rel.bearing absent.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives alone on the road: no vehicle meets it.

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions
param_proposals.source: heading tolerance of road-geometry alignment; lane-change heading angles

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition source

segmentation.text: Drivers of vehicles proceeding in opposite directions
shall pass each other keeping to the right,
and
upon highways having width for not more than one line of traffic in each direction,
each driver shall give to the other at least one-half of the paved portion of the highway
as nearly as possible.

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, for the subject and the other. 'proceeding in opposite directions': rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing'; its exclusion concerns the direction of approach to an intersection, which these words do not name. 'proceeding': the subject is not at rest (negation of drv.motion.complete_halt). 'Drivers' is read through the vehicles' controlled motion.

'highways having width for not more than one line of traffic in each direction': st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles', and st.lane_adjacency, 'the count of lanes in that direction', at most the stated figure, read on the lane the subject occupies (rel.occupies) on a highway (st.highway) it occupies.

'one-half of the paved portion of the highway': the half on the subject's side of st.centre_line, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway', of the way the subject is on (st.on_way, 'the public way … a structure region lies on'). 'give to the other': the subject's body stays on its own half: prim.region_lateral_offset of the centre line from the subject ('signed lateral offset … left positive') is at least half the subject's full width (kin.extent). 'the other' is the oncoming vehicle met: it closes on the subject within a horizon (prim.closest_approach_within, centres under constant velocities, not a contact or clearance) or is alongside (rel.longitudinal_overlap).

operationalizations.convention: The subject gives the other half of the paved portion as nearly as possible where its body crosses the centre line by no more than a lateral positioning tolerance p.lateral_position_tolerance, or where its body is already within that tolerance of the road edge on its right (st.road_edge, ground distance through st.region_geometry, on the right per prim.region_lateral_offset), so that no more room is available to it.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle that is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), occupying a highway (rel.occupies, st.highway) and a lane (st.lane) whose lane count in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count) is at most one.
obligation: For every road user c that is a vehicle, occupies the highway the subject occupies, is oncoming to the subject (rel.oncoming with p.oncoming_heading_cos) and is meeting it (prim.closest_approach_within(subject, c, p.meeting_horizon) or rel.longitudinal_overlap: projections share length), and for every centre line l lying on that highway (st.centre_line, st.on_way): prim.region_lateral_offset(l, subject) is at least half the subject's full width (kin.extent) less p.lateral_position_tolerance, or the subject's body is within p.lateral_position_tolerance of a road edge (st.road_edge, st.region_geometry distance) lying on its right (prim.region_lateral_offset negative). Violated where neither holds.

narrowings.why: 'Drivers' is read through the vehicles' controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls them.

'the paved portion of the highway' is read as the roadway the centre line divides; a paved shoulder is not added to either half. Its half is given while the other vehicle approaches within p.meeting_horizon or is alongside.
'as nearly as possible' is read through the subject's room to its right road edge; obstacles on the subject's half are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Two-lane two-way road; the moving subject car straddles the centre line by 1 m while an oncoming car approaches 2 s away, with 2 m of room to its right road edge.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same road; the subject car keeps its body right of the centre line as the oncoming car passes.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives on a highway whose lane counts two lanes in its direction.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Two-lane road with an oncoming car approaching; the source maps regions without their outline (st.region_geometry absent), so the offset from the centre line is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives over the centre line on a two-lane road with no other vehicle in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A very narrow paved road; the subject's body crosses the centre line by 0.5 m while its right side is at the road edge, as an oncoming car passes.

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions
param_proposals.source: heading tolerance of road-geometry alignment; lane-change heading angles

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition source

param_proposals.name: p.meeting_horizon
param_proposals.convention: the time ahead within which two vehicles closing head-on on a narrow two-way road count as meeting, so that each keeps to its half: the decision-and-steering time of a driver adjusting lateral position
param_proposals.source: AASHTO decision sight distance (avoidance manoeuvre times)

param_proposals.name: p.lateral_position_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the lateral margin within which a vehicle body counts as at a line or an edge: lane-keeping variability of a driven vehicle plus the source's position error
param_proposals.source: lane-keeping lateral deviation studies

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in subsection 2,
on a controlled-access highway
which has two or more clearly marked lanes for traveling in the same direction,
a driver may not continue to operate a motor vehicle in the extreme left lane
if the driver knows, or reasonably should know, that he or she is traveling at a rate of speed which is less than the posted speed limit for that portion of the controlled-access highway
and is being overtaken in that lane from the rear by a motor vehicle traveling at a higher rate of speed.
The requirements of subsection 1 do not apply: (a) To a driver operating a motor vehicle that is:
(1) Overtaking another vehicle proceeding in the same direction;
(2) Preparing for a left turn
at an intersection;
(3) Traveling in a lane designated for the use of high-occupancy vehicles pursuant to NRS 484A.460,
if the driver complies with the requirements to travel in such a lane
or (4) Engaged in the construction, maintenance or repair of the highway, including, without limitation, the removal of snow.
(b) When traffic conditions, inclement weather, obstructions or hazards
make it necessary to drive in the extreme left lane.
(c) When compliance with an official traffic control device or the directions given by a peace officer makes it necessary to drive in the extreme left lane.
(d) To the driver of an authorized emergency vehicle in the course of his or her official duties.
(e) To a driver operating a motor vehicle
within the geographical limits of a city or town.

elements.justification: st.controlled_access: 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes', DEF-NRS-484A-060's controlled-access highway; rel.occupies (which lists 'controlled-access lane') anchors it to the subject's footprint.

'two or more … lanes for traveling in the same direction': st.lane_adjacency, 'the count of lanes in that direction', at least the stated figure, read on the lane (st.lane) the subject occupies (rel.occupies). 'clearly marked': the lanes' presence on the map is the evidence (observable_reading status).

'a motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. 'in the extreme left lane': st.lane_adjacency, 'ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction', of the lane the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.lane). 'continue to operate' is the subject remaining there while the triggers hold, over the move-over window; 'driver' and 'operate' are read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'traveling at a rate of speed which is less than the posted speed limit for that portion': kin.speed below the value of a dev.speed_limit_sign ('sign stating a maximum or minimum speed, with value and unit'; kind maximum) that governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies): the limit of that portion. Same anchoring as 'unless a different speed limit is posted' (LVMC_11_16_060). 'knows, or reasonably should know' is read through those facts themselves (observable_reading perception).

'being overtaken in that lane from the rear by a motor vehicle': a road user c, a motor vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle), behind the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction'); 'traveling at a higher rate of speed': kin.speed of c above the subject's, so that c, behind in that lane, closes on the subject from the rear: the words read as they say.
'a driver operating a motor vehicle that is:' introduces the exceptions (1)-(4) for the subject, a motor vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle), carried by their own spans.

'Overtaking another vehicle proceeding in the same direction': drv.interaction.overtake_pass, 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it', with b a vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle); the overtaking is under way where its recognition falls within the window ahead of length p.overtake_window.

'at an intersection': st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet', DEF-NRS-484A-105's intersection; it is the target region at which the declared intention is read, bound by the intention's region quantifier.

'a lane designated for the use of high-occupancy vehicles': st.reserved_lane, 'lane reserved for a class of vehicles; class ∈ {high_occupancy, …}', class high_occupancy, occupied by the subject (rel.occupies). 'high-occupancy vehicles' borrows DEF-NRS-484A-460-2: '(a) A vehicle that is transporting more than one person; (b) A motorcycle, regardless of the number of passengers; (c) A bus, regardless of the number of passengers; and (d) Any other vehicle designated by regulation.' — the class for which the lane is reserved. 'designated … pursuant to NRS 484A.460' is read through the reserved lane's presence (observable_reading status).

'the requirements to travel in such a lane' are, by DEF-NRS-484A-460-2, the conditions the Department determines ('(1) The number of occupants required per vehicle; and (2) The hours of the day that the use of the lane is restricted') and advises on signs; the class of road user the lane serves is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-460-2::high_occupancy_vehicle, which borrows '(a) A vehicle that is transporting more than one person; (b) A motorcycle, regardless of the number of passengers; (c) A bus, regardless of the number of passengers; and (d) Any other vehicle designated by regulation.' The posted conditions are a dev.zone_sign of kind high_occupancy_lane governing (dev.governs) the reserved lane, its 'conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend'; that they hold for the subject is prim.conditions_hold, 'the structured conditions of a device … hold at the observation for a road user'. The sign's exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: whether the condition holds now' is met by reading prim.conditions_hold for it.

'Engaged in the construction, maintenance or repair of the highway, including … the removal of snow': the vehicle is in road service, ru.official_vehicle ('a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment'), kind highway_maintenance, and shows the conduct of a vehicle at work on the highway: an amber warning lamp lit, flashing or rotating (sig.warning_lamp, 'a warning lamp lit; colour ∈ {red, blue, amber, white}, mode ∈ {flashing, rotating, steady}'). Its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: an audible warning' does not apply; the class's exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' does not apply.

'traffic conditions': road users of the traffic (DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) occupying (rel.occupies) the lane to the right of the subject's (st.lane, st.lane_adjacency 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction'). 'inclement weather': env.precipitation ('rain or snow falling'), env.wet_road, env.ice_or_snow, env.visibility ('visibility distance (fog, dust, smoke)'). 'obstructions or hazards': st.obstruction ('a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user'), located from the subject by its ground distance (st.region_geometry) and its side (prim.region_lateral_offset, 'left positive'), never by a region-to-region relation.

'compliance with an official traffic control device … makes it necessary': a device governing (dev.governs) the lane to the subject's right (st.lane_adjacency) closes it: dev.lane_control_signal state red_x or yellow_x, dev.regulatory_sign code closed_to_traffic or do_not_enter, or dev.temporary_traffic_control ('cones, barricades … marking works, a closure'). 'the directions given by a peace officer': dev.human_direction role police_officer, indication stop, governing that lane. 'official' is read through the device's presence (observable_reading status).

'authorized emergency vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle, carried by ru.aggregate; the class alone is no conduct, so being 'in the course of his or her official duties' is read through the conduct of a vehicle operated on duty as an emergency vehicle: a warning lamp lit, flashing or rotating (sig.warning_lamp, 'a warning lamp lit … mode ∈ {flashing, rotating, steady}') or a siren sounding (sig.siren, 'a siren, whistle or bell sounding'); the source reads the two separately, as sig.siren's contract requires.
'a driver operating a motor vehicle': the subject, DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

operationalizations.standard: make it necessary to drive in the extreme left lane
operationalizations.convention: Stopping-distance convention: S = speed(subject) × H + speed(subject)² / (2 × D), with H and D selected by the surface (_ice where env.ice_or_snow, _wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation, else _dry), as for following distance. The left lane is necessary where moving right cannot be done within S: a traffic member occupying the right neighbouring lane has a longitudinal body gap to the subject (rel.surface_gap) below S, or an obstruction lies within ground distance S of the subject on its right (st.region_geometry, prim.region_lateral_offset negative), or the visibility distance (env.visibility) is below S. Each factor enters by degree: the subject's speed and the surface move S; the gap, the distance and the visibility are compared with it.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies within the geographical limits of an incorporated city or of a town, as the map's reading classifies the area

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

compositions.quote: (a) A vehicle that is transporting more than one person; (b) A motorcycle, regardless of the number of passengers; (c) A bus, regardless of the number of passengers; and (d) Any other vehicle designated by regulation.

residues.why: Points to subsection 2, which is appended to this same law line and carried by its own exception spans k8-k20; the duty is the same whether or not these words are read.

applicability: The subject is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) occupying a controlled-access highway (rel.occupies, st.controlled_access) and a lane (st.lane) that is the leftmost (st.lane_adjacency ordinal first) of two or more lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count at least two); it is not an authorized emergency vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle) showing a lit flashing or rotating warning lamp (sig.warning_lamp) or sounding a siren (sig.siren), and the reading does not place it within the limits of a city or town (not asm.within_city_or_town_limits).
obligation: Let S hold at an observation where: the subject occupies the leftmost lane of two or more in its direction on a controlled-access highway; its speed is below the value of some maximum dev.speed_limit_sign governing a travel region it occupies; and none of these holds: (1) within the window ahead of length p.overtake_window, drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, c, p.overtake_window, p.overtake_same_direction_cos) for some vehicle c; (2) intent int.left_turn of the subject at some intersection region; (3) the subject occupies a reserved lane r of class high_occupancy, is a high-occupancy vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-460-2::high_occupancy_vehicle), and prim.conditions_hold(z, subject) for every dev.zone_sign z of kind high_occupancy_lane governing r; (4) the subject is an official vehicle of kind highway_maintenance showing a lit amber warning lamp, flashing or rotating (sig.warning_lamp); (b) with S_stop = speed × H + speed² / (2 × D) (H, D selected by surface as in the operationalization), some traffic member occupies the lane to the right of the subject's lane with longitudinal surface gap below S_stop, or some obstruction lies within ground distance S_stop on the subject's right, or env.visibility is below S_stop; (c) a device governing the lane to the right closes it (lane control signal red_x or yellow_x, regulatory sign closed_to_traffic or do_not_enter, temporary traffic control, or police_officer direction stop). Let O hold where some motor vehicle c is behind the subject in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with speed above the subject's. Violated at an observation where, at every observation of the window behind of length p.left_lane_move_over_time, S has held at every observation since an observation at which O and S held together (holdsFor of since(S, O ∧ S)), and some motor vehicle is behind the subject in its lane at the judged observation.

narrowings.why: 'clearly marked' lanes are read through the lanes the map represents; the paint's clarity is not modelled.

'continue to operate' is read as the subject remaining in the leftmost lane, slower than the limit and unexcused, for the window p.left_lane_move_over_time after a faster motor vehicle closed on it from behind, with a motor vehicle still behind it in that lane; 'driver' and 'operate' are read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'knows, or reasonably should know' is read through the facts known: the subject's own speed and the posted maximum governing where it is.
The lane's designation pursuant to NRS 484A.460 is read through the reserved lane of class high_occupancy the map represents.

Being engaged in construction, maintenance or repair of the highway is read through the conduct of a highway-maintenance vehicle at work: its amber warning lamp lit, flashing or rotating; such a vehicle driving with no warning lamp lit is not excused.

'traffic conditions' and 'hazards' are read only through road users in the right neighbouring lane and obstructions on the subject's right; inclement weather only through the surface condition, falling rain and the visibility distance.
An 'official' device is read through its presence on the road.

'in the course of his or her official duties' is read through the conduct of an emergency vehicle on duty: a warning lamp lit, flashing or rotating, or a siren sounding. An authorized emergency vehicle on duty that shows neither is not excused.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Three-lane controlled-access highway outside city limits (asm.within_city_or_town_limits false), dry; a maximum speed sign of 29 m/s governs the lanes. The subject car drives in the leftmost lane at 24 m/s; a car approaches from 80 m behind in the same lane at 32 m/s, closes and then follows at 24 m/s; the subject stays in the leftmost lane for 30 s with the middle lane empty.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject signals and moves to the middle lane 5 s after the faster car closes from behind.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives in the middle lane at 24 m/s with a faster car behind it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same scene as forbid; the source declares dev.speed_limit_sign absent, so whether the subject is below the posted limit is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Same scene with the reading placing the highway within city limits (asm.within_city_or_town_limits true).

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; a lane control signal showing red_x governs the middle lane throughout, closing it.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives in the leftmost lane at 24 m/s with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: The subject is an authorized emergency vehicle with its warning lamps flashing, driving in the leftmost lane at 24 m/s with a faster car closing from behind.

scenarios.name: branch_5
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the middle lane is occupied by a truck travelling alongside the subject at a body gap of 5 m throughout, so moving right is not possible.

param_proposals.name: p.left_lane_move_over_time
param_proposals.convention: the time a driver needs, once a faster vehicle closes from behind, to check the mirrors, signal and move one lane to the right: a perception-reaction time, a few seconds of signal and the lane change
param_proposals.source: lane-change duration studies; driver manuals (signal at least 3 s before a lane change)

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_window

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as travelling in the same direction while one moves out to pass the other
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading angles

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_dry
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on a dry surface: the two-second rule of driver manuals
param_proposals.source: state driver handbooks

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_wet
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on a wet surface or in rain: the two-second rule lengthened by a second
param_proposals.source: state driver handbooks

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_ice
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on an icy or snow-covered surface: the tripled following time driver manuals advise
param_proposals.source: state driver handbooks

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_dry
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a dry paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.6)
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book; tyre-road friction tables

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_wet
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a wet paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.4)
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book; tyre-road friction tables

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_ice
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on an icy or snow-covered surface (coefficient of friction about 0.1)
